Summer Music Retreat 2026 Upper Bhagsu


Unveil Your True Musical Potential — Upper Bhagsu, Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh

Most people believe they cannot sing. They are wrong.

In 10 days in the Himalayas, you will discover a voice you never knew you had — and a practice that stays with you for life.

Krishna Music School — teaching authentic Indian music to seekers from over 50 countries since 2007

Picture this: mountain mist rolling over Upper Bhagsu at dawn, the deep green of Himalayan forests all around, the sound of a waterfall in the distance, and your own voice — finally — finding notes it has never found before.

That moment happens here. Every year. For students who arrived convinced they had no musical talent whatsoever.

This is Krishna Music School’s Summer Retreat — running for 12 consecutive years in the Himalayas, now open for 2026 with three batch options. It is a genuine, structured 10-day transformation for people who want to go deep into Indian music, their own voice, and themselves.

Why the Himalayas Change Everything

You could learn these techniques anywhere. But you would not learn them the same way.

Upper Bhagsu sits above the bustle of McLeod Ganj, cradled in a valley of deep pine forests and cascading streams. The greenery here is extraordinary — terraced hillsides, the Bhagsu waterfall roaring through cedar trees, birds calling from the ridges at dawn. This is the setting in which your voice opens up. It is not coincidence. It is the Himalayas doing what they have always done.

With three batch options — April, May, and June — you can choose the dates that fit your travel. Each batch offers the same full 10-day curriculum with fresh mountain air and lush greenery as your backdrop. April arrives with spring blossoms, May brings the forests to their richest green, and June offers warm Himalayan days before the full monsoon settles in.

What We Teach — and Why It Works

Your Voice Is Not Broken. It Is Untrained.

The single most important thing we do in the first session: we stop you from singing the way you think you should sing, and we show you how your voice actually works. Most people have spent their whole lives either avoiding their voice or forcing it. Neither produces music. Neither produces joy.

At Krishna Music School, we have spent 17 years developing techniques — what we call god-gifted methods — that cannot be written in a book or watched in a video. They require a teacher in the room, listening to you specifically, adjusting for your voice specifically. That is what makes this retreat irreplaceable.

Real teaching, real connection — no screens, no algorithms, just voice and presence

In 10 days you will learn to consciously use:

  • Your belly, chest, and throat for natural, effortless breath support
  • Your jaw, mouth, and tongue to place each of the seven notes precisely
  • Your hands, head, and eyes for genuine musical expression and feeling
  • Your harmonium — playing and singing together, in rhythm and in tune

Your 10 Days — What Actually Happens

Days 1–2: Finding Your Foundation

Everything in Indian music begins with Sa — the root note, your anchor in the scale. For the first two days we focus here completely. Not because it is simple, but because without a stable Sa, nothing else holds.

You will learn Sargam (Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni Sa), correct breath placement, and where tension hides in your voice. By Day 2, your own voice will sound different to you. Cleaner. More yours.

Day 3: Your Body Is the Instrument

Your voice does not live in your throat. It lives in your entire body. On Day 3 we teach you exactly how to coordinate belly, chest, hands, head, and eyes while you sing. This is where technique becomes feeling — where sound becomes music. Until this coordination is correct, true emotional expression cannot come.

Days 4–5: Mouth Positions + Harmonium

Inside your mouth are seven distinct resonance points — one for each note. Knowing where to place each note transforms voice quality overnight. These adjustments are small. Their impact is enormous.

Then the harmonium enters. Playing the scale with your hands while singing it with your voice. Challenging at first, profoundly satisfying when it clicks.

Day 6: Palta — From Notes to Music

Advanced note patterns that build coordination, clarity, and musical flow. This is the day students feel the shift from practicing exercises to actually making music. You are no longer learning rules. You are beginning to speak a language.

Days 7–10: Mantra, Kirtan, Bhajan & Raga

Everything converges. You will chant mantras for Shiva, Krishna, Hanuman, Ganesh, Rama, Kali, Radha, Guru, and the Gayatri — each with its own energy and feeling. You will sing bhajans, lead kirtan with proper melody, rhythm, and devotion, and discover how raga — the emotional architecture of Indian classical music — creates different states of being. On the final day, a full group temple tour through Dharamshala’s sacred sites.

What You Leave With

  • Voice control and breath stability — sustain notes without effort or wavering
  • The 7-note mouth placement system — transform your tone from the inside
  • Harmonium fluency — play melodies and accompany your own singing
  • Palta and Alankar technique — the building blocks of classical Indian voice training
  • Mantra chanting with feeling — correct pronunciation, melody, and devotion
  • Kirtan and Bhajan skills — lead chanting, build energy in a group
  • An introduction to Raga — understand how melody creates emotion
  • A daily practice — something to return to every morning for the rest of your life

Common Questions

I genuinely cannot sing. Will this work for me?

That is exactly who this is designed for. 90% of our students arrive with no musical experience at all. Our techniques are built around the absolute beginner — not because we have lowered the standard, but because we have spent 17 years learning how to unlock voices that have never been properly taught. You will feel the difference from Day 1.

Which batch should I choose — April, May, or June?

All three batches run the same full curriculum. April offers spring freshness and lighter crowds. May brings the forests to their most lush and vivid. June is warm and vibrant though early monsoon showers may arrive toward the end. Choose based on your travel dates — all three are excellent.

I am traveling solo. Will I feel out of place?

Solo travelers are the majority at every retreat. The small group format (maximum 10 students) makes connection natural and fast. Past retreats have seen students from 8 countries in a single group stay in touch for years afterward. You will leave with friendships, not just skills.

Why two sessions per day instead of one longer class?

A morning session followed by a full day of rest, exploration, and natural absorption — then an evening session to consolidate — is far more effective than one long class. Your brain and voice need space between learning and practicing. The split schedule is deliberate and it works.

Can I join for fewer than 10 days?

The retreat is a progressive journey — each day builds directly on the last. Partial attendance weakens the experience significantly. If your travel window is shorter, we run private classes year-round at our main campus in Pushkar, Rajasthan.

Are private instrument classes available during the retreat?

Yes. Private classes for Tabla, Dholak, and Violin are available alongside the retreat. Contact us to arrange a schedule that fits your afternoons in Dharamshala.

What language are classes in?

All instruction is in English. Our teachers have 12 years of experience teaching international students from over 50 countries. They know exactly how to make ancient techniques clear to every kind of learner.

About Krishna Music School

Founded in 2007 near Rangji Temple in Pushkar, Rajasthan, Krishna Music School has taught authentic Indian classical music to students from over 50 countries for 17 years. The Upper Bhagsu Summer Retreat has run continuously for 12 of those years. Our teachers work in the traditional guru-shishya lineage — patient, precise, and deeply committed to every learner’s journey.

Beyond the summer retreat, we offer tabla, dholak, violin, and guitar at our Pushkar campus, plus intensive programs of 30, 60, and 90 days for students who want to go deeper. Many retreat alumni return the following year — not because they need to, but because they want to.
